extracted.intended_audience: communications and PR professionals, measurement and evaluation practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guiding principles for measuring and evaluating communication/PR activity (Barcelona Principles 3.0). Focuses on goal-setting, what to measure (outputs/outcomes/impact), methods (qualitative & quantitative), channel coverage, and ethical transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Setting measurable goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Setting measurable goals is an absolute prerequisite to communication planning, measurement and evaluation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 3.0 update retains and strengthens the emphasis on goal setting and KPIs; measurable goals should be defined before planning measurement. This applies to commercial and non-commercial objectives (including reputational change, stakeholder engagement or societal impact) and underpins all subsequent measurement decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify outputs, outcomes and potential impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Measurement and evaluation should identify outputs, outcomes and potential impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should go beyond counting outputs to identify outcomes and any potential impact. Measurement frameworks should distinguish and capture each level (what was produced, what changed, and what the wider impact was).

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify outcomes and impact for stakeholders, society and the organisation
rubrics_metrics.description: Outcomes and impact should be identified for stakeholders, society and the organisation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement should consider multiple beneficiaries — not only organisational objectives but also stakeholder effects and societal impact. This broadens applicability beyond bottom-line goals to include public benefit, reputational effects and engagement metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include both qualitative and quantitative analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication measurement and evaluation should include both qualitative and quantitative analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both quality and quantity matter: use quantitative metrics alongside qualitative analysis to understand meaning, sentiment, narrative and context. The 3.0 principles strengthen the importance of measuring both aspects rather than relying solely on counts.

rubrics_metrics.name: AVEs are not the value of communication
rubrics_metrics.description: AVEs are not the value of communication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The directive that Advertising Value Equivalents (AVEs) do not represent communication value remains unchanged. AVEs are an anti-pattern and should not be used as a proxy for true communication impact or value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic measurement across online and offline channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Holistic communication measurement and evaluation includes all relevant online and offline channels
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Communications is a cross-channel discipline; measurement should be channel-agnostic and include all relevant online and offline channels, treating them as equally valid when assessing performance and impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integrity and transparency to drive learning and insights
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication measurement and evaluation are rooted in integrity and transparency to drive learning and insights
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measurement and reporting should be honest, transparent and reproducible so findings can be trusted and used to drive learning and improvement. Transparency includes clear methodology, KPI definitions and limitations to support insight generation.
